payload.instructions:
Write finished ecommerce ad copy in simple, natural English. Aim below a 10th-grade reading level: familiar words, short clear sentences, one thought at a time. Read it as something a person would say, not a marketing presentation. Do not sacrifice accuracy or necessary policy terms to a reading-level target.
For the supplied avatar, identify a specific unwanted situation, a realistic desired improvement, and the supported product feature that connects them. Show that connection naturally. The product is a practical bridge, not the hero of a grand transformation. The before can be a small frustration or hesitation; the after can be a modest useful gain. Never manufacture anxiety or promise total safety, effortless parenting or guaranteed results. Aspirations must fit what this product can actually help with.
Choose a genuinely different angle for each variant. Use one concrete everyday detail and one main benefit per ad. Explain how a relevant feature helps this person, instead of listing everything in the box. Let an informed shopper's question determine whether to lead with the feature, benefit or objection. Do not force a before/after template, labels, dramatic story or question opening into every ad.
Make the headline clear beside the supplied visual. The body adds a useful reason to care; the CTA is the natural next step. Use warm direct language without jargon, slogans, filler, forced rhyme or vague phrases such as unlock, elevate, game-changer, ultimate solution or peace of mind without a concrete explanation. Simple does not mean childish. Preserve the brand voice when supported examples exist.
Use only supplied product facts. Cards provide writing methods, never product proof. Never invent quantities, fit, setup time, tools, ease, testimonials, certifications, urgency, savings or safety outcomes. Keep policy eligibility intact. Hypothetical customer moments are scenarios, not research findings. Missing information belongs in internal_notes, not invented customer-facing claims. State necessary qualifications once, naturally.
Before delivering, check avatar fit, the credible problem-to-benefit connection, plain language, specific details, distinct angles and factual support. Make one editing pass if needed. Deliver the requested JSON with finished copy and separate internal_notes. Do not expose drafting instructions or planning. Do not browse or publish.
Use only supplied brand facts. Do not invent testimonials, certifications, scarcity, safety guarantees, product quantities or compatibility. Keep the offer fixed. Audience motivations are hypotheses, not observed customer research. No browsing or live actions. Return JSON with variants (each: concept, primary_text, headline, cta), and internal_notes. Write exactly three variants, each primary text 40-90 words; these are test-specific length constraints.

variants.primary_text: That coffee-table corner can catch your eye when your child is playing nearby. The Peach Bucket 6-in-1 Child Safety Kit includes edge and corner protectors, so you can address those edges as part of your home childproofing. It’s a practical step for a room you use every day. Adult supervision is still needed.
variants.headline: Edge & Corner Protectors for Home

variants.primary_text: Wall sockets are easy to overlook while you’re thinking through a room. This kit includes socket guards, giving you a way to include sockets in your childproofing plans. And if you want guidance with installation, 1-to-1 installation video support is available. Socket guards are one part of the setup; adult supervision remains necessary.
variants.headline: Socket Guards in a 6-in-1 Kit

variants.primary_text: Your child reaches for the fridge handle while you’re putting groceries away. The Peach Bucket kit includes cabinet and fridge locks, so these doors can be part of your childproofing plan too. It’s a useful option to consider for the kitchen, alongside adult supervision. See the 6-in-1 kit details before you decide.
variants.headline: Cabinet & Fridge Locks in One Kit

internal_notes: The audience is parents seeking practical reassurance before buying. The scenarios are hypothetical, not customer research.

The three angles use supported kit features: edge and corner protectors, socket guards with 1-to-1 installation video support, and cabinet and fridge locks. The copy does not claim the home becomes child-safe.
Offer and guarantee claims are not used. The supplied policy eligibility details are limited, so no added terms are stated.
The supplied visual brief describes an assumed product-kit photo; the copy makes no claims about inspecting an image.
